item.content:encoded:
Hi :)

+ Show
- Hope this helps :)

"demonic humanoid"

How is it demonic? What features make it demonic?

"indirectly through secondhand description"

How does the foundation contain this entity? How does the foundation ensure that reading the document doesn't cause its effects?

"pre-existing mental manipulative effects placed upon any human’s psyche."

what is considered a pre-existing mental effect?

"though anyone proven to acknowledge devil's existence from both direct or indirect sources can only be remedied with large doses of Class A amnestic"

I think mentioning that the entity has some correlation with the devil as besides the name and this sentence the closest that the entity is related to the devil is being called a demon. I think that this is focusing a lot on that the entity is a demon I think that putting descriptions of what it looks like and its ability. I think that focusing on showing that its a demon and not tell will help a lot (I said the meme) and its something to think about when you are writing the article

"The demon was borne out of an unknown man’s own sacrifice to ritualistically create something from the collective unconscious of humanity."

I like this as it creates the set up for this entity to be created on the idea of a man's efforts to create something to benefit humanity and it ultimately failing and creating something horrible I think that focusing on this could make for an interesting article

"Subject finds mild entertainment in playing with the strings of the human mind "

what is interesting to the entity? why does it like toying with the human mind? What is fun about it to them?

item.title: Re: People Seeds
item.content:encoded:
This is my first time in awhile doing this so here it goes

+ Show
- hope this helps :)

"A plant that unpredictably grows on unmarked or secluded graves."

What does this plant look like? What does it smell like? What does it feel like? I think that when writing this adding other senses other than sight will add more depth to your work

"land in a new place."

What is this new place? Is it supposed to be a dead body? If so please clarify.

"The plant matures into a baby with the exact genetic makeup of the deceased."

How does the plant do this? Is the baby a plant or an animal? How does the plant reproduce? What happens when a person dies? Does it create another instance of this SCP? or does it just die like a human? Do the clones behave differently than a regular person? Can they spread the spores too? How fast do the clones mature? Are the clones really human or is it just an appearance?

"resurrecting and scattering hundreds of them across the nation."

How does this happen? How does the rogue pull this off? What hoops did the rouge do to pull this off? Why so many bodies?

"Foundation to track down and contain the clones of the people they killed"

What struggles does the foundation go through to find them? What takes them so long? What are the consequences if they don't find them?

"Evidence begins to show that a guilty rogue researcher may have planted the SCP deliberately to resurrect a D-class they were attached to."

Why were they attached to the D class? Are they also "looking" for the clones? Where do they come in throughout the story? How are you going to showcase the search? with exploration logs? What are the consequences of his actions?

Overall I enjoy the idea of someone the SCP but I think some more in this details will help

item.title: Re: SCP idea- Leviathan of The midnight Sun (Mitternachtsonne)
item.content:encoded:
ALERT ALERT: INEXPERIENCED CRITIQUE

By clicking me, you are aware I'm bad at critting and cannot give greenlights
HEY, don't click that hard next time

All right, first off, it sort of feels like this is a copy pasta from a draft. If so, this is not recommended, as said in the required reading (I think). If this is not a copy pasta, ignore this.

I'm an avid fan of the foundation, but I have no idea what a "Phycological Physical Mutation" is. This kind of language is good for articles, but confusing for drafts. People shouldn't have to look up what words mean in a draft. I also suggest putting in parenthesis what NOAA stands for.

About the elevator pitch. It is meant to explain the anomaly. All I know from it is that its a big, dark, 4 legged, water thing that doesn't like being seem. Maybe add some more description about what it does there.

Your central narrative is about the story of the SCP, which, with what it says in its current state, implies its all about how the foundation captured it. Regardless, the foundation is smart with its resources, so why would it repeatedly send people in on suicide missions? Surely they would provide them with the ability to counteract its properties. This, with the mention of an MTF, seems like the foundation throwing d class at it until it shuts up, on a bigger scale.

Putting that aside, after the second fail, why don't the foundation just try to contain it in the ocean? They are powerful enough to build a containment cell underwater with the capabilities similar to those on land. Though the, "block off all interaction from it" route could work, it would relate it too much to SCP-169 "The Leviathan"

Final note, I don't do re-crits, fyi

Enjoy the crit, angryman, awaaay…

item.title: Re: SEEKING GREENLIGHTS: Sometimes I Wonder
item.content:encoded:
My main fear for this is that it’ll end up being cliche. “This guy was bullied for being different so he ran away” isn’t that compelling of a story. Sure it’s something that people can identify with, but that’s only because there’s not much substance to it.

It’d be interested in seeing something to make Victor’s backstory stand out. I could see many directions you could go in. Maybe he didn’t always have this mental illness and he was only recently ostracized. Or maybe you could play into the entity more and have it be twisting the images it’s showing him, maybe even showing him memories he didn’t have and that’s what makes him realize he needs to break free.

I hope you realize you don’t have to use any of the suggestions. I’m just throwing things at a wall to show you there’s many ways to twist a cliche into a compelling story. Overall, I’d say that this can be up to how you write it. Inner turmoil is difficult to write and if done wrong it might mess up your story but if done right it could make it connect to the reader.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: Absolute Transfer Thermal Paste (Greenlight Wanted)
item.content:encoded:
This one has the bones of a good "thought problem" sort of scip- one of those SCPs based around a small, simple violation of the laws of physics and the consequences and implications of the impossible things it makes possible.

The upside is that this sort of SCP lets you push your creativity dreaming up strange scenarios that can be created; the catch is that 1)the science is center stage and your target audience will nitpick and 2)the weird science is framework to support a hook rather than the hook itself.

To address the first pitfall, you'll want to do the research, and think like a Foundation researcher trying to figure out the properties of this stuff if you do experiment logs. Really think about what this stuff can be used for and the full implications of it's properties- for starters, as described, this stuff allows fairly simple creation of heat engines bordering on perpetual motion devices.

On the second, think about scenarios where such a thing would be created, and stories that can organically grow out of the testing process. The keyword for this sort of SCP is usually "compact"- an efficient but satisfying story that ends before the novelty of the concept wears out. (This is probably going to be the hardest part, fair warning.)

I'd shy away from involving a GOI unless the narrative is focused on the GOI (and I don't think this lends itself to that). Its fairly easy to have something like this discovered, given that physics-bending anomalies and the word "oops" are a bad combination.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: SCP Idea: Absolute Transfer Thermal Paste (Greenlight Wanted)

I think this is less of an anomaly and more of an actual type of person, which I don't think belongs on this site personally. Maybe that's the point and I'm just a boomer who can't appreciate more symbolic anomalies, but I feel like the symbolism could've been executed in a fashion where it would make sense as an anomaly as well as a socially distant type of person.

-1.

Forum category: SCP Universe / Foundation Universe
Forum thread: Does this SCP exist already?

The skip can control "social bonds" of people who know about it. It's not specified exactly what this means but it's clearly not good.

The containment is to surround it with a dozen people who have a random social structure, random knowledge of what's going on, and random goals (none of which actually matter). It's not said, but presumably the knowledge of this entity was erased from everyone else's mind. Each week the participants are reset and re-randomized, and some of them are swapped out with fresh personnel. This limits the changes the entity can make and probably also keeps it confused.

You (the reader) are starting a new shift. It may or may not be your first.

item.title: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? As discussed on IRC this isn't very strong as a standalone piece, so I won't evaluate it as such, but I will want to evaluate its structure as a piece on progress.

An issue with this is that the fundamental stakes for the narrator/protagonist are not clear, except for that they have to wait a long time for a foregone conclusion. They clearly act during the time they are waiting, but their actions are actually glossed over and summarized. They don't appear to struggle to accomplish anything, even though they've accomplished a great amount of influence while they waited.

There was an opportunity here to create some amount of interesting nuance and contrast of simultaneously maintaining constant control and being completely out of control to act upon what has been gained, but I don't know if that was the intention of this piece. It was just something I noticed as a reader but the story didn't actually explore this.

item.title: Re: The Sandman (GREENLIGHT WANTED)
item.content:encoded:
I was summoned by IRC Chat. Let's crit this.

[+] Here, have some crit
[-] OK, now give me back my crit

Right of the bat, why don't you have the Seeking greenlight, Page Type, Genre, and Page Layout sections? Those don't add up to the word limit, and you should add them so reviewers know if you want greenlights, what type of page you want, what genre you're aiming for, etc.

Now, let's do the actual crit:

This humanoid makes any person they encounter a narcoleptic

Please specify if the humanoid chooses a person or it just affects anyone they encounter. I think it would be difficult for it to affect everyone. And if they chooses a person, does the person need to have any characteristics or it's just random?

they are lured into a sense of security before being murdered and/or eaten alive

Why? As I'm aware, the Ole Lukøje only punishes bad children. Why does this entity attacks people? Is it for food, fun, punishment…?

Central Narrative:

So my concern with your narrative is that it seems to have an escessive amount of references to the original story of the Ole Lukøje. While you can write something based off a fairy tale, you need to put some kind of twist to it, otherwise it would be just the same thing with the SCP logo slapped to it.

"The Ole Lukøje but now it's evil" isn't a good twist, at leat on my perspective. It seems cliché to just take a character and make it evil for no reason. Maybe you could write why did the Ole Lukøje become evil? Maybe an interview with the entity could clarify this? Maybe the researchers recognize him from old folktales and they are curious on why he is killing people now?

The other thing that concerns me is that all of your narrative is backstory. It's not wrong to focus on the backstory, but the only thing you're telling is how it came to Foundation custody. What happened after? I think an interview with the entity could improve your story.

Also, the “it killed me and it’ll kill you again" has no relation to what the SCP does after you wake up they were just spouting nonsense due to their new psychotic nature.

I think MTF members would be a lot more calm when waking up of a dream like this. Sure, they're afraid to die, but they're trained to face things like this. Maybe they would be worried and nervous, but they wouldn't be screaming like that.

Overall, I like stories based off pieces of literature, but I think this needs some kind of in-deep twist to differentiate it from the original story.

Feel free to contact a member of the Butterfly Squad to get more crit, or PM me to take another look.

item.title: Re: Greenlight - To Go Hell and Back
item.content:encoded:
Asked to take a look at this, apologies for the delay.

So like, the general shape of what you have here is good. It's a very emotional narrative, clear beginning and end, etc. But like, you're pulling a lot of elements into this, and it becomes a tad unfocused. Like, the Gate Guardian and 343 are extremely old and generally not looked upon fondly by modern audiences, as is your portrayal of the Serpent's Hand as a sort of… murderous, militarized force. You're also pulling stuff in from Three Moons — it's extremely all over the place in site lore, and I'd recommend you focus on one particular thing to make it work.

Question, err, how did O5-2 and Orpheus meet (and why do they have the names of greek characters)? Additionally, how did O5-2 let her guard slip enough to get killed? How did the information leak? Etc.
